title: Casper and the Horizon
premise: Ulyana Galloway navigates the freighter Casper along a dead trade route, carrying two hundred cryosleeping colonists—refugees from a war both their homeworlds pretend never happened. When a distress call arrives in Pre-Diaspora Standard, a language extinct for two centuries, Ulyana traces it to a derelict station orbiting a star that shouldn't exist, and finds the signal's source is a third faction of humanity everyone believed annihilated: the ones who stayed behind. As the station's failing reactor begins a countdown that will either jump-start the Casper's dead drive or consume both ships, the sleeping colonists' backups start waking on their own, each carrying memories Ulyana's employers paid to bury. Ulyana must choose whether to wake the colonists as themselves or restore the sanitized versions their sponsors intended, and in the final hours gives the sleepers the truth—letting them vote on who they will be—before riding the reactor's surge through the horizon of a star that was never supposed to burn.
about_author: Lior Hartwell is a former maritime cartographer who turned to science fiction after a decade charting coastlines that keep disappearing from the maps. They write about people who carry places inside them, and live between two port cities that no longer share a language.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine run between the silent worlds of Meridian and Vask opens the book: cargo, silence, and the hum of two hundred sleepers in the hold whom Ulyana is contractually forbidden to wake. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as competence—Ulyana talks to the ship because no one else answers.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Casper intercepts a repeating distress transmission in Pre-Diaspora Standard, a language Ulyana knows only from a grandmother's lullabies. Protocol says ignore it; the melody in it says otherwise. The beat is recognition—the first time in years Ulyana feels addressed rather than merely employed.

chapters.title: The Station That Shouldn't Orbit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana diverts to a station around an uncharted star, finding hulls grown, not built, and air that tastes of home. A surviving caretaker intelligence, Ashen, greets them in the dead tongue. The beat is vertigo: history Ulyana was taught ended is still breathing.

chapters.title: Backups in the Hold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ulyana and a sleeper's backup, Sefa, who wakes without authorization and remembers a version of the voyage Ulyana never lived. Sefa reveals the colonists' memories were edited before freezing. The beat is betrayal—Ulyana realizes they've been guarding a lie, not a cargo.

chapters.title: What Meridian Paid For
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Digging through the ship's sealed manifests, Ulyana uncovers the contract: the colonists are a settlement experiment whose 'failure' was pre-written, and the Casper's route exists to keep them from ever arriving. The beat is cold fury and the first taste of choice.

chapters.title: Ashen's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. The station intelligence explains why it called: its reactor can recharge the Casper's dead jump drive, but only by venting the station's atmosphere—and Ashen has been alone for two hundred years deciding whether anyone was worth the cost. The beat is grief meeting hope.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The reactor cycle begins early, destabilized; Ulyana has hours, not days, and the drive will take only one ship's worth of charge—station or Casper, not both. Meanwhile more backups wake, fracturing into factions over whether to trust Ulyana. The beat is accelerating dread.

chapters.title: The Vote of the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Sefa's POV. Ulyana breaks the contract and wakes the colonists, restoring their true memories from Sefa's hidden archive, then puts the choice to them: take the charge and abandon the station, or split the power and risk both. The beat is the book's moral heart—belonging means being asked.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. The colonists vote to share the charge; Ashen compresses itself and the station's archive into a seed-pod to survive. Ulyana threads the Casper through the reactor's surge, burning the ship's hull to carry both cargoes of memory through. The beat is sacrifice that refuses to be tidy.

chapters.title: A Language With Speakers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, resolution. Damaged but alive, the Casper limps toward a world no one speaks for, carrying Ashen's seed, two hundred awake colonists, and a contract Ulyana has publicly voided. In the final scene, Ulyana teaches the colonists the lullaby in the dead tongue—and it is no longer dead. The beat is quiet, earned belonging.
